newsitem.title: USA: First State declares $0.09 div after split.
newsitem.headline: First State declares $0.09 div after split.

text.p: Note: Full name of company is First State Corp
The company also said it had approved a 3-for-2 stock split; the new cash dividend reflects that stock split.
The company said its dividend increased by 22.73 percent and marked the fifth consecutive year the company had announced such a rise.
Morgan Murphy, chairman and chief executive of First State, said the increase in cash dividend was a result of strong financial performance for the 1996 calendar year.
During 1996, the company said, First State earned more than $7.5 million with a return on average assets of 1.63 percent and a return on average equity of 16.72 percent.
In the first quarter of 1997, First State earned $0.38 per share with a return on average equity of 14.97 percent, and a return on average assets of over 1.43 percent, the company said.
